title: io_uring Submission Queue Entry (SQE)
summary: An io_uring SQE is a 64-byte structure submitted to the kernel via the submission queue ring. It encodes the operation (opcode), flags, file descriptor, offset, buffer address/length, and user data. The kernel reads SQEs from the SQ ring and completes them into CQEs.

ext.summary: An io_uring SQE is a 64-byte structure submitted to the kernel via the submission queue ring. It encodes the operation (opcode), flags, file descriptor, offset, buffer address/length, and user data. The kernel reads SQEs from the SQ ring and completes them into CQEs.

structure.meaning: Operation: 0 NOP, 1 READV, 2 WRITEV, 3 FSYNC, 4 READ_FIXED, 5 WRITE_FIXED, 5 IORING_OP_POLL_ADD, 6 POLL_REMOVE, 7 SYNC_FILE_RANGE, 8 SENDMSG, 9 RECVMSG, 10 TIMEOUT, 11 TIMEOUT_REMOVE, 12 ACCEPT, 13 ASYNC_CANCEL, 14 LINK_TIMEOUT, 15 CONNECT, 16 FALLOCATE, 17 OPENAT, 18 CLOSE, 19 FILES_UPDATE, 20 STATX, 21 READ, 22 WRITE, 23 FADVISE, 24 MADVISE, 25 SEND, 26 RECV, 27 OPENAT2, 28 EPOLL_CTL, 29 SPLICE, 30 PROVIDE_BUFFERS, 31 REMOVE_BUFFERS, 32 TEE, 33 SHUTDOWN, 34 RENAMEAT, 35 UNLINKAT, 36 MKDIRAT, 37 SYMLINKAT, 38 LINKAT, 39 MSG_RING, 40 FSETXATTR, 41 SETXATTR, 42 FGETXATTR, 43 GETXATTR, 44 SOCKET, 45 ... .
IOSQE_FIXED_FILE (1<<0), IOSQE_IO_DRAIN (1<<1), IOSQE_IO_LINK (1<<2), IOSQE_IO_HARDLINK (1<<3), IOSQE_ASYNC (1<<4), IOSQE_BUFFER_SELECT (1<<5), IOSQE_CQE_SKIP_SUCCESS (1<<6).
File descriptor (or fixed-file index if IOSQE_FIXED_FILE).
File offset for read/write; or secondary address for some ops.
Pointer to buffer / iovec array / pathname, depending on opcode.
Op-specific flags (e.g. read/write flags, poll events, accept flags).
Opaque value echoed back in the CQE; used to correlate completions.
Fixed buffer index or buffer group for IOSQE_BUFFER_SELECT.
Registered personality (credentials) index, or 0 for current.
Third address (renameat new path, xattr name, etc.).

ext.example_decoded: NOP SQE (opcode 0), all zeros except user_data
notes: SQEs are 64 bytes; the kernel reads them from the SQ ring (mmap'd).
The SQ ring is a single-producer (application) / single-consumer (kernel) ring buffer.
IORING_SETUP_SQE128 doubles SQE size to 128 bytes for larger operations.
Fixed files (IORING_REGISTER_FILES) avoid repeated fdget/fdput overhead.
Buffer selection (IOSQE_BUFFER_SELECT) lets the kernel pick a buffer from a registered group for recv/read.
